title: Vector Symbolic Algebras (VSA) Workshop: Neural Computation & Robotics Applications
summary: This page describes a workshop on Vector Symbolic Algebras (VSAs), originally termed Vector Symbolic Architectures. The session covered theoretical foundations including high-dimensional vector spaces, pseudo-orthogonality, and fractional binding for probabilistic modeling. It highlighted applications in robotic control, model predictive control, and active learning, noting efficiency gains over standard methods like Gaussian process regression. VSA was presented as a bridge between symbolic AI and connectionist dynamics suitable for neuromorphic edge devices by reducing memory costs associated with tensor products. The workshop discussed running these computations on physical analog hardware and their emergence in large language models.
tldr: A theoretical workshop explored Vector Symbolic Algebras (VSAs) to enable efficient probabilistic modeling, robotic control, and interpretable neural computation for neuromorphic edge AI applications.
